title: Singer Phil Dooley and the Southland record
summary: Coquille knew little about Phil Dooley, who sang on a Southland record, and they discuss whether a banjo is on it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Back to your records, too. Another thing. Who was Phil Dooley? I never did know him. He sang with Norman?

Well, Joe Merez knew Phil Dooley. I hadn't known him until a record session. I don't know if he's from New Orleans, but he came down and he did one of these Southland records with us. And he sang, if I remember right, on the recording. And Joe Merez knew him real well. I didn't know Phil Dooley until I cut the record.
But did you know if he was an emcee or? He just sang. That's all you knew about him, huh?
I don't even know. I don't even remember if Phil played a musical instrument. I think he just sang. I think he just sang with the band.
There's so many people like that around him.
So many of the emcees did sing.
I don't even know if Phil Dooley was from New Orleans.
Did you have that Southland record?
And one of the books says it has a banjo on it, but I never heard the banjo.
